digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, App. V, App. VI

teaser.en: A fern that keeps the water in the bucket: its fronds float on top to stop it splashing on the carrier's head.

summary.en: Mvwiko is Davallia chaerophylloides, a lacy fern. Its fronds are laid on the water in a bucket carried on the head, as floaters that stop it spilling.

about.en: Mvwiko is a fern with a thick, creeping rhizome covered in brown scales, from which finely divided, lacy, triangular fronds arise. The tiny spore cases sit in small cups near the edges of the leaflets. The Digo identify it by its leaves.

where.en: It grows on tree trunks, rocks and shaded banks in moist forest and thicket.

uses.en: Pakia records that the leaves are put into a bucket of water as floaters (mivwiko) to keep the water from spilling onto the person carrying it on her head.

culture.en: Pakia lists Mvwiko among names that describe a plant's product, alongside Msabuni (soap) and Msuwaki (toothbrush).

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name Mvwiko, meaning 'floaters', after the mivwiko placed in water buckets. The same name is used for bracken, Pteridium aquilinum. Pakia's English name is simply 'fern'; its scientific name is Davallia chaerophylloides.

reason.en: Also named after a household product
Another plant that grows on trees
